body.message:
The root decision is where the speech actually comes from, because it shapes everything else. Marky Mark runs in a system webview (WKWebView on macOS, WebView2 on Windows), and in-webview speech recognition (the web SpeechRecognition API) is unsupported/unreliable there — so the realistic prototype paths are:

How should Marky Mark get the words + commands?
options: Layer on top of your existing dictation — you keep using whatever dictation you already have (macOS Dictation, Wispr Flow, etc.) typing into the editor, and Marky Mark watches text land and rewrites recognized spoken command phrases into markdown. No mic access, works with any dictation tool. (recommended)

Marky Mark owns the mic and runs its own speech recognition via a native platform ASR plugin (Tauri/Rust) — full real-time control separating commands from content, but heavy, per-platform, and needs mic permissions.
Marky Mark owns the mic via the in-webview web SpeechRecognition API — lightest to build but unsupported/flaky across the macOS + Windows webviews.
Something else / I want to talk through the trade-offs first.
